dayTrips.title: The Wild West Coast
dayTrips.subtitle: From Lagos to Sagres via dramatic cliffs and surfer beaches

route.tip: Start here early (8am) for best light and no crowds. Walk the full clifftop path.
Stop at the viewpoint before descending. The beach bar does excellent fresh fish.
Coffee stop at Sitio do Forno. This is where serious surfers base themselves.
Watch the surfers from the cliff if you're not surfing. The energy here is special.
Time arrival for golden hour. The last light seller packs up authentic local honey.
Walk the full perimeter walls. The wind is always fierce — bring a jacket.

whereToEat.lunch: Castelejo Beach Bar (fresh fish, terrace views) or bring a picnic

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round, but spring/autumn for hiking. Winter for dramatic waves (watching only!).

dayTrips.title: Ria Formosa & Eastern Algarve
dayTrips.subtitle: Island beaches, fishing villages, and the authentic Algarve

route.tip: Arrive by 9am for the market at its best. Saturday is peak. Buy fish to grill for locals.
Take the ferry to Culatra village, walk across the island to Praia da Culatra beach. Pure paradise.
This is where you eat. Casa do Polvo is famous, but any waterfront restaurant is excellent.
Climb the castle hill for sunset views. Walk across the Roman bridge for photos.
A tiny whitewashed village overlooking the lagoon. One of the most photogenic spots in the Algarve.

whereToEat.lunch: Casa do Polvo Tasquinha in Santa Luzia (book ahead)

dayTrips.bestSeason: Year-round. Summer for beaches, spring/autumn for walking, winter for birdwatching.

dayTrips.title: Mountain Escape
dayTrips.subtitle: Monchique, Silves, and the interior Algarve most tourists miss

route.tip: Enter the castle first thing. Walk the walls for 360° views. The town below is perfect for coffee.
The natural springs are free to drink. Walk the shaded forest paths. Very peaceful.
Try medronho (local firewater) and buy local honey. The main square has great views.
On clear days you can see both coasts. Temperature drops 8-10°C from the coast — bring layers.

whereToEat.lunch: A Eira do Mel in Monchique (huge portions, mountain food)

dayTrips.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers, summer to escape beach heat, autumn for mushrooms.

dayTrips.title: The Secret Beaches Drive
dayTrips.subtitle: Cliff coves and hidden gems between Lagos and Carvoeiro

route.tip: Park at Dona Ana lot, walk south. The tunnel connecting beaches is magical.
The tunnel carved through the cliff is the entrance. Arrive early — it's small and fills fast.
Book a 7:30am kayak tour for empty cave. Or come in winter for solitude.
Often overlooked because it's not on main routes. The natural arch is stunning.
End the day here for sunset. The wine bar at the boardwalk has perfect positioning.

whereToEat.lunch: Rei das Praias near Carvoeiro or picnic on the cliffs

dayTrips.bestSeason: May-October for swimming. Year-round for exploring.

dayTrips.title: Seville Day Trip
dayTrips.subtitle: Over the border to Spain's most romantic city

route.tip: Leave by 8am. The A49 highway is fast and well-maintained. Fill up before crossing — Portuguese gas is cheaper.
Book tickets online in advance. Go first thing when it opens — crowds build fast.
Get intentionally lost. The best tapas bars are hidden in the maze.
Climb the Giralda tower — it's a ramp, not stairs. Worth it for the views.
Late afternoon light is best for photos. The ceramic benches represent each Spanish province.

whereToEat.lunch: El Rinconcillo (oldest tapas bar in Seville) or any Santa Cruz spot
whereToEat.coffee: Confitería La Campana for traditional pastries

dayTrips.bestSeason: Spring (March-May) or autumn (Sept-Nov). Avoid July-August — Seville is brutally hot.
